profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne cluster sits in the Cincinnati metro area, spanning Cincinnati, Lebanon, and Butler and Warren Counties in Ohio and Florence, Kentucky just across the Ohio River. This is CyrusOne home market: Wikipedia coverage states Cincinnati Bell purchased CyrusOne for 525 million dollars in 2010 and later divested its remaining stake in 2015 after the company IPO in 2013. CyrusOne was originally founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten. The company was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CIN6 in Florence, Kentucky publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, making it the state's largest facility by public record, though only one of five Kentucky sites discloses a megawatt figure at all.

The facility spans 143,000 square feet of technical space, a ratio of roughly 28,600 square feet per megawatt. This density suggests design for moderate rather than high-density compute. At 10 kW per rack, typical of enterprise colocation, 5 MW would support approximately 500 racks. At 40 kW per rack, the density common in AI training, it would support roughly 125 racks. The operator publishes neither actual rack count nor power density, so these remain assumptions about the floor's current use.

CIN6 holds certifications for payment card data, protected health information, federal information systems, and enterprise workloads. Green Globes indicates environmental performance assessment. None of these certifications directly address AI workloads, and no tenant information is public. The facility qualifies to host regulated enterprise data but offers no signal about AI-specific infrastructure or tenancy.

At 5 MW, CIN6 is small relative to hyperscale AI campuses now routinely publishing figures above 100 MW. Kentucky has no major concentration of published AI-oriented capacity. This is a regional enterprise colocation facility, not a primary destination for large-scale AI training infrastructure by the numbers currently available.
